00011| Welcome to the Next.js documentation!
00012| 
00013| ## What is Next.js?
00014| 
00015| Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.
00016| 
00017| It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.
00018| 
00019| Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
00020| 
00021| ## How to use the docs
00022| 
00023| The docs are organized into 3 sections:
00024| 
00025| - [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
00026| - [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
00027| - [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
00028| 
00029| Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
00030| 
00031| ## App Router and Pages Router
00032| 
00033| Next.js has two different routers:
00034| 
00035| - **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
00036| - **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
00037| 
00038| At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
00039| 
00040| ### React version handling
00041| 
00042| The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
00043| 
00044| - **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
00045| 
00046| - **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
00047| 
00048| This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
00049| 
00050| ## Pre-requisite knowledge
00051| 
00052| Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
00053| 
00054| - HTML
00055| - CSS
00056| - JavaScript
00057| - React
00058| 
00059| If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
00060| 
00061| ## Accessibility
00062| 
00063| For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
00064| 
00065| ## Join our Community
00066| 
00067| If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).
00068|

00019| Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
00020| 
00021| ## How to use the docs
00022| 
00023| The docs are organized into 3 sections:
00024| 
00025| - [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
00026| - [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
00027| - [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
00028| 
00029| Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
00030| 
00031| ## App Router and Pages Router
00032| 
00033| Next.js has two different routers:
00034| 
00035| - **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
00036| - **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
00037| 
00038| At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
00039| 
00040| ### React version handling
00041| 
00042| The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
00043| 
00044| - **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
00045| 
00046| - **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
00047| 
00048| This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
00049| 
00050| ## Pre-requisite knowledge
00051| 
00052| Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
00053| 
00054| - HTML
00055| - CSS
00056| - JavaScript
00057| - React
00058| 
00059| If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
00060| 
00061| ## Accessibility
00062| 
00063| For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
00064| 
00065| ## Join our Community
00066| 
00067| If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

If [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request. 00053| - **`no-store`**: Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request, even if Request-time APIs are not detected on the route. 00054| - **`force-cache`**: Next.js looks for a matching request in its server-side cache. A request matches on its URL, method, headers, and body, so requests that differ in any of these are cached separately. 00055| - If there is a match and it is fresh, it will be returned from the cache. 00056| - If there is no match or a stale match, Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server and updates the cache with the downloaded resource. Only responses with a `200` HTTP status code are stored. 00057| 00058| > **Good to know**: Caching is opt-in. Set `cache: 'force-cache'` to cache any request, including `POST` and requests that send `authorization` or `cookie` headers. [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) bypasses the cache entirely (no read or write). 00059| 00060| ### `options.next.revalidate` 00061| 00062| ```ts 00063| fetch(`https://...`, { next: { revalidate: false | 0 | number } }) 00064| ``` 00065| 00066| Set the cache lifetime of a resource (in seconds). 00067| 00068| - **`false`** - Cache the resource indefinitely. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity`. The HTTP cache may evict older resources over time. 00069| - **`0`** - Prevent the resource from being cached. 00070| - **`number`** - (in seconds) Specify the resource should have a cache lifetime of at most `n` seconds. 00071| 00072| > **Good to know**: 00073| > 00074| > - If an individual `fetch()` request sets a `revalidate` number lower than the [default `revalidate`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config-revalidate) of a route, the whole route revalidation interval will be decreased. 00075| > - If two fetch requests with the same URL in the same route have different `revalidate` values, the lower value will be used. 00076| > - Conflicting options such as `{ revalidate: 3600, cache: 'no-store' }` are not allowed, both will be ignored, and in development mode a warning will be printed to the terminal. 00077| 00078| ### `options.next.tags` 00079| 00080| ```ts 00081| fetch(`https://...`, { next: { tags: ['collection'] } }) 00082| ``` 00083| 00084| Set the cache tags of a resource. This is separate from persistent [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching): memoization lasts only for a single render pass, while cached responses persist across requests. 00089| 00090| To opt out, pass an [`AbortController`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController) signal to `fetch`: 00091| 00092| ```js 00093| const { signal } = new AbortController() 00094| fetch(url, { signal }) 00095| ``` 00096| 00097| > **Good to know**: Memoization does not apply in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), since they are not part of the React component tree. 00098| 00099| ## Troubleshooting 00100| 00101| ### Fetch default `auto no cache` and `cache: 'no-store'` not showing fresh data in development 00102| 00103| Next.js caches `fetch` responses in Server Components across Hot Module Replacement (HMR) in local development for faster responses and to reduce costs for billed API calls. 00104| 00105| By default, the [HMR cache](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) applies to all fetch requests, including those with the default `auto no cache` and `cache: 'no-store'` option. This means uncached requests will not show fresh data between HMR refreshes. However, the cache will be cleared on navigation or full-page reloads. 00106| 00107| See the [`serverComponentsHmrCache`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) docs for more information. 00108| 00109| ### Hard refresh and caching in development 00110| 00111| In development mode, if the request includes the `cache-control: no-cache` header, `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, and `options.next.tags` are ignored, and the `fetch` request is served from the source. 00112| 00113| Browsers typically include `cache-control: no-cache` when the cache is disabled in developer tools or during a hard refresh. 00114| 00115| ## Version History 00116| 00117| | Version | Changes | 00118| | --------- | ------------------- | 00119| | `v13.0.0` | `fetch` introduced. | 00120| (End of file - total 120 lines)

| Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. | 00040| | `delete(name)` | - | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie. | 00041| | `toString()` | String | Returns a string representation of the cookies. | 00042| 00043| ### Options 00044| 00045| When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported: 00046| 00047| | Option | Type | Description | 00048| | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 00049| | `name` | String | Specifies the name of the cookie. | 00050| | `value` | String | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie. | 00051| | `expires` | Date | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire. | 00052| | `maxAge` | Number | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds. | 00053| | `domain` | String | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available. | 00054| | `path` | String, default: `'/'` | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain. | 00055| | `secure` | Boolean | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security. | 00056| | `httpOnly` | Boolean | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access. | 00057| | `sameSite` | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior. | 00058| | `priority` | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority | 00059| | `partitioned` | Boolean | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). | 00060| 00061| The only option with a default value is `path`. 00062| 00063| To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies). 00064| 00065| ## Good to know 00066| 00067| - `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies. 00068| - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. ---
title: cookies
description: API Reference for the cookies function.
---

`cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).

```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

export default async function Page() {
  const cookieStore = await cookies()
  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
  return '...'
}
```

```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.

## Enabling Cache Components

You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:

> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.

Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.

## Enabling Cache Components

You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:

---
title: Server and Client Components
description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-client
    - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary
---

By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.

This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.

> **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).

## When to use Server and Client Components?

The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.

---
title: Server and Client Components
description: Learn how you can use React Server and Client Components to render parts of your application on the server or the client.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned in this page.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-client
    - app/guides/server-and-client-boundary
---

By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.

This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.

> **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).

## When to use Server and Client Components?

The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.

- This is Next.js 16 canary with the App Router. `Cache Components` is **not** enabled (empty `next.config.ts`), so the previous caching model applies.
